title: metadata-admin declares an object "provided by an installed package, so it is read-only" even in a writable package — Studio treats the same object as editable and the server accepts the PUT
body:
## Symptom

Three surfaces disagree about whether one object is editable.

For an object published into a **writable** package:

- **metadata-admin designer** shows the artifact-locked banner — *"This {type} is provided by an installed package, so it is read-only at runtime. To change it, edit it in its source package and republish — or create a new {type} from scratch."*
- **Studio** treats the same object as **editable**.
- **The server accepts the PUT.**

So the banner asserts a lock that neither the other console pillar nor the runtime applies. An operator who believes it goes off to "edit it in its source package and republish" for a change they could have made in front of them.

## Root cause (located)

The banner is gated on metadata-admin's own artifact-backed heuristic in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx`:

```
… layered.code != null
  && (layered.code as { _packageId?: string } | null)?._packageId !== 'sys_metadata';
```

— lines 951-955, repeated at 1311-1323, where the comment states the intent: *"artifact-backed items (`layered.code != null`) need allowOrgOverride … Mirror the server's `isArtifactBacked` (which excludes `_packageId === 'sys_metadata'`)"*. The banner string is `i18n.ts:864`.

The heuristic asks only "is there a code layer, and is it not the `sys_metadata` sentinel". An object published into a **writable** package satisfies both — it has a code layer, tagged with that package — so it is classed artifact-backed and locked in this pillar, even though the writability question the other two surfaces answer is a different one (is *this package* writable), and they answer it yes.

**Stale-premise check:** re-verified on `objectui` `origin/main` (`33c32bf`) — both heuristic sites and the banner string are present and unchanged.

## Relationship to #4036 — same disagreement, opposite direction

#4036 reports the mirror case: in a **code-defined (read-only)** package, Studio disables editing for all 15 overlay-allowed types while the runtime accepts those writes, and a "writable" badge sits on a screen of disabled controls. This card is the same class with the polarity flipped — a **writable** package where metadata-admin claims read-only while Studio and the server say editable.

Taken together they argue for one shared writability predicate rather than three per-surface heuristics: today each pillar derives the answer independently, so both false-positive and false-negative lockouts exist simultaneously in the same console. Whoever rules on #4036's question A should rule on this at the same time — the two cards will otherwise get opposite answers.

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase and publish an object into a **writable** package.
2. Open that object in the metadata-admin designer → the "provided by an installed package, so it is read-only at runtime" banner is shown.
3. Open the same object in Studio → it is presented as editable.
4. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/<name>` with the full body → the server accepts it.

## Source

Extracted from the QA run objectstack-ai/objectstack#7695 (framework 92f26f75, console 09987b680) — "Corrections and notes" item 5, split out of the consolidated notes card because the three-way disagreement is a product defect rather than a run note.
